title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The document records a decision taken by the AI Office regarding a specific policy or operational change. It outlines the rationale, scope, and intended impact of the decision in plain terms.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document announces a vacancy for technology specialists in AI, outlining the need for professionals with expertise in artificial intelligence technologies. It details the qualifications, responsibilities, and application process for interested candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This policy announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI office. It outlines the responsibilities, qualifications, and application process for the role.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy announces a new vacancy for Legal Officers in the AI office, detailing the role’s purpose and how it supports the organization’s AI initiatives. It outlines the required qualifications, key responsibilities, and the application process for interested candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The document announces a vacancy for Policy Officers in the AI Office, detailing the roles and responsibilities of the position. It explains the qualifications required, the application process, and what the organization expects from candidates.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts that reviews and advises on the EU’s AI regulatory framework, ensuring that the rules are technically sound and aligned with scientific standards. They evaluate proposed rules, identify risks, and recommend safeguards to protect public interests while fostering innovation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This policy outlines how an organization can formally request the creation or adoption of new standards for AI systems. It details the criteria for eligibility, the submission process, review timelines, and the roles of stakeholders in ensuring that the standards are developed transparently and consistently.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation on creating a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI. It invites stakeholders to give feedback on how the CoP should be structured and what policies and guidelines it should adopt.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for people to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy. It invites potential members to submit their interest so they can be considered for participation and collaboration within the group.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This policy explains how the Community of Practice uses a graphic to illustrate its iterative drafting process, highlighting continuous feedback and collaboration. It outlines the stages of drafting, review, and revision that guide the development of clear and comprehensive policies.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document presents a visual timeline that outlines the stages and key dates in the drafting of the AI policy, helping stakeholders see the sequence of events and milestones. It highlights phases such as consultation, drafting, review, and approval, indicating when each was completed and the next steps to follow.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document outlines the initial set of guidelines for responsible AI practice, establishing core principles and expectations for stakeholders. It serves as a starting point for developing standardized, ethical AI operations and encourages further refinement and collaboration.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document outlines the second draft of a Code of Practice for responsible AI development and deployment. It provides guidelines and best‑practice standards to help organizations ensure ethical, transparent, and accountable use of AI technologies.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The document outlines a set of guidelines for how organizations should develop, deploy, and monitor AI systems in a responsible and ethical way. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and risk mitigation so that AI is used safely and fairly across different sectors.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft outlines commitments by governments, industry, and civil society to develop and deploy artificial intelligence responsibly, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It proposes guidelines and collaborative frameworks aimed at mitigating risks while promoting ethical standards and inclusive benefits from AI technologies.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final establishes a collaborative agreement among governments, industry, and civil society to guide the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It sets out principles for transparency, safety, fairness, and ongoing cooperation to help AI technologies benefit society while minimizing risks.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This document lists the AI activities that are disallowed to keep technology safe, fair, and lawful. It bans practices that could deceive people, cause harm, or violate privacy and ethics, such as deepfake creation, autonomous weapon use, or biased decision-making systems.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: These guidelines explain what counts as an AI system, outlining the key features and technical components that qualify a system under the policy. They also describe how to classify and document AI systems to ensure consistent use of the policy across organizations.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The policy outlines ways to improve communication and support for startups and innovation, aiming to help new businesses grow faster and more effectively. It focuses on building networks, sharing best practices, and creating a supportive ecosystem that encourages collaboration and access to resources.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups is a European effort to give early‑stage companies access to high‑performance computing resources. It offers startups training, funding, and collaboration opportunities so they can develop and scale AI and data‑intensive solutions.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar provides an overview of risk management principles and best practices. It covers key strategies for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks in organizational contexts.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This is a video webinar that focuses on risk management. It covers how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks in various contexts.
